current_answer: Current evidence supports several distinct routes: fal H3 Max Director is a finite hosted context-carrying WebRTC session; Yoroll says H3 Superfast powers YoLive, a group proposal-and-vote route; Reactor FastH3 is a high-end queue-and-playout route; FastVideo documents local FastH3 clip paths and a four-GPU Dreamverse frame-carried Preview v1 profile; a community project reports one RTX 5090 sustaining a retimed dense FastH3 channel; Comfy offers local H3 paths; and vLLM-Omni documents a separate H3 service. The new vLLM-Omni workflow boundary is client scope: its serving recipe documents ordered first-and-last-frame conditioning, while its current H3 API/ComfyUI RFC says the current ComfyUI client accepts only one FL2VA frame and limits some reference combinations. Treat a server feature, a client feature, and a recorded workflow as separate facts. The two-RTX-5090 full-H3 record remains one 50-step T2VA validation: 124 frames at 1344×768 / 24 fps, about 5.17 seconds of output, returned in 8 minutes 38 seconds with at least 200 GiB available host RAM. It is an offline capacity result, not a first/last-frame, live, or transition route.

catalogue_card.question: Can vLLM-Omni’s ComfyUI client send first and last H3 frames?
catalogue_card.text: Not yet, according to its current H3 parity RFC. The server recipe documents ordered first-and-last-frame conditioning, but the current client accepts one FL2VA frame and limits some references. Do not confuse the endpoint with the workflow.

summary: vLLM-Omni’s H3 serving recipe documents ordered first-and-last-frame FL2VA inputs, while its current H3 API/ComfyUI parity RFC says the current ComfyUI client accepts one FL2VA frame.

The RFC says the server supports T2VA, first-frame FL2VA, mixed Ref2VA, repeated references, reference ordering, and H3 reference limits; the current client caps each reference modality at two inputs and rejects some valid mixed-reference combinations.
The RFC lists work to add first/last-frame and broader reference support. It is an open plan, not proof of a shipped or tested client workflow.

The two-RTX-5090 full-H3 record remains one 50-step T2VA capacity validation: 124 1344×768 / 24 fps frames, about 5.17 seconds of media, returned in 8 minutes 38 seconds. It does not prove a two-keyframe workflow.
uncertainty: vLLM-Omni’s client-scope statements come from an open project RFC and recipe documentation. The pool did not install the server or client, inspect actual requests, or test first/last-frame or mixed-reference output.
The reported two-RTX-5090 result is one project-published T2VA validation. The pool did not independently audit its environment, media, timing, or quality.

The 8 minutes 38 seconds result is client end-to-end for one run, not a warmed multi-run result. It does not establish first frame, streaming, queue, concurrent requests, retries, uptime, cost, or viewer-visible latency.
The two-5090 target validation does not establish FL2VA or Ref2VA. vLLM-Omni’s eight-B300 FastH3 result is a different, warmed dedicated T2VA profile.
Dreamverse’s FastH3 profile is project documentation; the pool did not install or run it, inspect a generated handoff, or measure buffer, cost, recovery, or uptime.
FastVideo and ComfyUI still conflict on FastH3 8-Step V2 FL2VA scope. The pool did not run a pinned T2VA or FL2VA workflow.
No pool test, invoice, uptime log, end-to-end source-to-visible latency measurement, or first-party pool analytics is available.
freshness_note: Checked 25 September 2026. The new workflow limit is client scope: current vLLM-Omni H3 documentation separates a server that can express richer conditioning from a ComfyUI client that cannot yet send both FL2VA keyframes. No pool test has verified either path.
